facts.fact: The Assistant Minister of Health told Parliament on 5 March 2026 that Phase 1 of the centralised Electronic Medical Record had been implemented in 22 health facilities in Ngami, to be extended to 21 facilities in Okavango by end of March 2026; the facility types and a national denominator are not given.

The Ministry of Health's 2026/27 budget speech reports the Phase 1 rollout of the centralised EMR as ongoing, at 22 facilities in Ngami to date, 21 more in Okavango due by end of March 2026 and the remaining 29 districts planned for the 2026/27 financial year.

The Ministry of Health's 2026/27 budget speech states that the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Local Government and Traditional Affairs will jointly roll out the completed EMR system to the remaining 29 districts in 2026/27.

The 2026/27 development budget request allocates P62,534,000 to the Ministry of Health headquarters for consultancies, computerisation and fleet, naming the 'Digitalization of Health Services Project' among what it funds; the EMR rollout is reported under the speech's 'Digitalisation of Health Services' heading, and the line does not name the EMR itself.
